decision: Merge only the isolated, matched-wheel observer metric projection after two paired campaigns. Observer mean gains repeat; retain independent shallow snapshot and exact legacy fallback. No universal mean/tail speedup or copy elimination is claimed.

build_control.method: Isolated control and prototype wheels built with identical production uv/maturin settings; control binary is byte-identical to preceding production native. Merged Rust/Python source and wheel native exactly match measured prototype.

environment.gc: enabled; collected before each measured batch
environment.io: warm OS page cache; no fsync; final buffer drain included
environment.memory: fresh-process Linux RSS, including native allocations

environment.io: warm OS page cache; no fsync; final buffer drain included
environment.memory: fresh-process Linux RSS, including native allocations

regression_surfaces: Metadata exclusion, insertion order, key/value reference identity
Shared summary/backend snapshot isolated from alerts original row

limitations: One independent shallow metrics dictionary is still allocated; not a reduction in copy count or end-to-end zero-copy.
Series and summary still separately scan/update their domains; no projection cache or fused observer publication is introduced.
Backend mean improves 9.72% then 10.47%, rules mean 7.18% then 7.35%.
Five-metric mean worsens 1.12% then 1.38% (~0.14-0.17 us/op); no claim that every path is faster.
Backend p99 worsens in both campaigns (111.70 to 117.12 and 110.25 to 114.48 us); rules p99 improves in both.
NumPy p99 initially worsens then improves in confirmation; tails are not universally preserved.
Local hundred-metric and span algorithms do not use this observer projection; no local/span speedup is attributed to it.
